title: The Rag King – 2D dark fantasy action game (in development)
author: Kafilette
selftext:
Hey everyone,



I've been working on this game on my own for a while now and finally put together a trailer, so I wanted to share it here.



It's called The Rag King. It's a 2D dark fantasy action game. The idea is pretty simple: the war is lost, the throne is taken, and everyone thinks the king is dead. He isn't. He crawls out of a pile of bodies with just his sword and tries to take his kingdom back.



Right now the game has sword and bow combat, a few bosses, abilities and charms you pick up as you go, and some NPCs with voiced lines. Still a lot to do though, so things will probably change.



A few things I spent way too much time on: the lighting in the dark areas, the boss fights, and the charm system.



To be upfront about it: I used AI tools for some of the visuals and voices and then reworked them to fit the game. I also use an AI assistant when coding. The trailer is recorded in-game and edited by me.



Would be great to hear what you think. Good or bad, both help.



Trailer: [https://youtu.be/ojgvEgMCvWc](https://youtu.be/ojgvEgMCvWc)

comments.author: Offbeat_voyage
comments.body: Love the atmosphere and the vibe feels dark and mysterious and autumn

replies.author: Kafilette
replies.body: Thanks for the comment. I'm really trying to take care of the story, the music and the environment design. It's a genre I love, so I'm doing my best to make something good out of it.

replies.author: Kafilette
replies.body: Thanks for the comment. I'm actually a designer myself, but producing every asset for a whole game alone is really tough. I take the images I get from PixelLab and rework them in Photoshop and Illustrator to fit the atmosphere as much as I can before adding them to the game. I'll definitely pay attention to the details you mentioned.

replies.author: TheLastCraftsman
replies.body:
It's not a joke, but perhaps poorly worded.  Having too many details in one area and then obvious flaws in another area is a major detriment to quality and is mostly the reason people dislike the AI slop.

Looking at the skeleton knight boss enemy for instance, there are way more details and frames than any human being would ever draw, but the animation is too rigid.  He should bob up and down as he walks and his legs bend.  No matter how good the quality of each frame is, it ruins the whole thing if they don't all work in concert.  Someone who COULD draw that well wouldn't make such an obvious mistake.

Making it look overly detailed in some areas with obvious flaws in others is a dead giveaway that the developer didn't care enough to do it properly.  If they didn't do that properly, then they probably didn't do everything else properly either.  At least that's what people will assume.

replies.author: Kafilette
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback. It’s definitely a work in progress, so insights like this are really helpful for the development process. I’ll keep working on it...

replies.author: Kafilette
